scores.evidence: Both mermaid diagrams (s1-diagram, s3-diagram) use flowchart TD. At 390 px they show readable Japanese labels with no clipping (pages/mobile-jp-04.png, pages/mobile-jp-12.png, pages/mobile-jp-13.png). The code blocks s2-skill, s3-file and pr-model show their highlighted frontmatter clearly on both viewports (pages/mobile-jp-06.png, pages/mobile-jp-14.png, pages/mobile-jp-23.png).

metrics.json reports no text-only screens on either device, and the full-length mobile PNG shows an even rhythm of headings, definitions, figures, code and checks with no wall of text. Desktop chars per line has a median of 39, inside the 30–40 target (max 56).

All text and diagram labels are Japanese, with English glosses where intended (スキル（skill）, フォーク（fork）). Contrast holds in the callouts, the quiz cards and the dark code blocks. No control is hidden under the 56 px top bar or the 60 px bottom bar (pages/mobile-jp-10.png, pages/mobile-jp-31.png).

niceToHave: section practice: on mobile the heading '演習：自分の手順をスキルにし、調べものを任せる' breaks as 'スキルに / し、調べものを任せる', so the second line starts with 'し、' (pages/mobile-jp-18.png). A shorter title such as '演習：スキルを作り、調べものを任せる' would avoid the split.

check-quiz e1: at 390 px, options 1 and 2 wrap inside their path chips at 'api- / guide/SKILL.md' (pages/mobile-jp-24.png). The paths still compare well because the '~/' vs '.' difference stays on the first line. A shorter skill name such as `api` would keep each chip whole.

s2-skill: on mobile, source line 12 ('1. `git status` と `git diff HEAD` で、') soft-wraps so that 'で、' sits alone on the next row (pages/mobile-jp-06.png). Moving 'で、' to the start of line 13 would keep each source line on one row.
reader: the end banner says 'このコースの最後のレッスンまで読み終えました。' because drafts are not listed in course.json (pages/mobile-jp-31.png, pages/desktop-jp-21.png). This is expected for drafts.
reader: the full-length mobile PNG stops at 16000 px. The per-screen PNGs cover the whole lesson.
summary: This preview shows lesson version sha256:d414e3e1a2e0ec5b, and all the global checks pass: no horizontal overflow, console errors, mermaid errors, unknown blocks or broken images. Diagrams, code blocks and quizzes are readable at 390 px and on desktop, and no screen shows personal data. Nothing needs to be fixed; the most useful polish is to rename the practice heading so the mobile line no longer breaks before 'し、'.
